title: Best Poker Hand
statement:
You hold five cards: card `i` has rank `ranks[i]` and suit `suits[i]`. Using any of these cards, decide which of the following hands you can form, ranked from strongest to weakest, and return the name of the strongest one exactly as written (capitalisation matters):

1. `"Flush"`: all five cards share one suit.
2. `"Three of a Kind"`: three cards share one rank.
3. `"Pair"`: two cards share one rank.
4. `"High Card"`: a single card, always possible.
constraints: No two cards have both the same rank and the same suit
notes:
## Intuition

The four hands are checked from strongest to weakest, and the first one that is possible is the answer. Whether a hand is possible depends only on how often suits and ranks repeat, so counting is enough: one suit used five times means a flush, and the largest rank count decides between three of a kind, a pair and a high card. A brute force could test every pair and triple of cards, which also works here because there are only five cards.

## Approach

1. Count each suit in `suitCount`. If only one suit appears, return `"Flush"`.
2. Count each rank in `rankCount` and keep `most`, the highest count seen.
3. If `most` is at least 3, return `"Three of a Kind"`; if it is 2, return `"Pair"`; otherwise return `"High Card"`.

## Example 1, step by step

`ranks = [13, 2, 3, 1, 9]`, `suits = ["a", "a", "a", "a", "a"]`. Every suit is `"a"`, so `suitCount` has a single key with count 5 and the function returns `"Flush"` before looking at the ranks.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): five cards, a fixed number of steps (O(n) for n cards).
- Space: O(1): at most 4 suits and 13 ranks are counted.

## Pitfalls

- Four cards of one rank still make `"Three of a Kind"`, so test `most >= 3`, not `most === 3`.
- Check the flush first: it beats every other hand.
- Return the names exactly as given, with the same spaces and capital letters.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `suitCount` | how many cards have each suit |
| `rankCount` | how many cards have each rank (index = rank) |
| `most` | the largest count of any one rank |

narration.2: Prepare a counter for the suits.
narration.4: Add one to that suit's count.
narration.6: If only one suit was seen, all five cards share it.
narration.7: That is a flush, the strongest hand.
narration.10: Ranks run from 1 to 13, so an array of 14 counters indexes them directly.
narration.11: most will hold the largest number of cards with one rank.
narration.14: Keep the largest rank count so far.
narration.17: Three or four cards of one rank make three of a kind.
narration.20: Exactly two of one rank make a pair.
narration.23: No rank repeats, so only a high card is left.
